rules.description: Applicant must have parental responsibility for the child
rules.reason_if_failed: You must have parental responsibility to apply for a child arrangements order. This includes mothers, fathers with parental responsibility, or certain relatives.

rules.description: Applicant must have attended a MIAM unless exempt
rules.reason_if_failed: You must attend a Mediation Information and Assessment Meeting (MIAM) before applying to court, unless you qualify for an exemption.

rules.description: Child must be habitually resident in England or Wales
rules.reason_if_failed: This service is for children habitually resident in England and Wales. Different rules apply in Scotland and Northern Ireland.

rules.description: Application is not an urgent safeguarding matter requiring immediate intervention
rules.reason_if_failed: This case requires immediate intervention. You should contact emergency services or social services.

edge_cases.description: Applicant has evidence of domestic abuse
edge_cases.action: MIAM exemption granted. Application fast-tracked. Cafcass safeguarding checks required. Special measures may be available in court (e.g. separate waiting areas, screens).

edge_cases.description: Child is at risk of harm or social services are involved
edge_cases.action: MIAM exemption granted. Immediate referral to Cafcass for safeguarding assessment. Court may order Section 37 investigation. Application prioritized.

edge_cases.description: One parent lives overseas or child may be taken abroad
edge_cases.action: May require prohibited steps order to prevent removal from jurisdiction. Check Hague Convention applies. Consider urgent 'without notice' hearing.

edge_cases.description: Allegations of one parent turning child against the other
edge_cases.action: Cafcass will conduct detailed assessment. Court may order psychological evaluation. Child-inclusive mediation recommended.

edge_cases.description: One or both parents have significant mental health issues affecting care
edge_cases.action: Cafcass assessment required. Court may request medical evidence. Specialist reports may be ordered.
